a: Change a query's predicate logic
d: Change the web server's TCP port
Create a JavaScript browser event handler
Authenticate a TLS certificate
e: A tautology may alter SQL filtering or authentication logic if it enters query syntax. Reflection of the string alone does not prove injection.
p: Payload purpose and successful execution are different claims.

q: Which of the following modes describes a wireless interface that is configured to passively grab wireless frames from one wireless channel and pass them to the operating system?
a: Monitor Mode
d: Managed Mode
Ad-hoc Mode
Master Mode
Repeater Mode
e: Monitor mode lets a wireless interface passively capture all 802.11 frames in the air.

q: Why is a fixed universal packet count unreliable for WEP key recovery?
a: Recovery depends on traffic, IV distribution, tools, and method
d: A single packet always reveals every WEP key
WEP has no IV in its frame format
The SSID length fixes the number of required packets
e: Statistical recovery depends on the evidence and algorithm used. Historical packet-count rules are approximations rather than guarantees.
p: Practical attack requirements are conditional.

q: Which attack exploits the predictable initial sequence number in older TCP implementations?
a: TCP Sequence Number Prediction Attack
d: TCP SYN Flood
TCP Reset Attack
TCP ACK Storm
TCP Sliding Window Attack
e: TCP sequence-number prediction exploits predictable ISNs in old stacks to spoof or hijack connections.

q: Which option makes the Apache httpd binary print its version?
a: httpd -v
d: httpd -k stop
httpd -M
httpd -S
e: The -v option reports version; -M lists modules and -S reports virtual-host configuration. Distribution binary names can differ.
p: Command flags answer different inventory questions.

q: In which file on a Unix system would you find hashed user passwords if shadow passwords are not in use?
a: /etc/passwd
d: /etc/shadow
/etc/group
/etc/secure
/etc/login.defs
e: Without shadowing, the hashed passwords sit in the world-readable /etc/passwd, easy to grab and crack offline.

q: Which of the following Nmap switches would you use to perform a UDP scan?
a: -sU
d: -sS
-sT
-sP
-sX
e: nmap -sU performs a UDP scan.

q: Which protocol does not support encryption by default?
a: FTP
d: HTTPS
SSH
SFTP
FTPS
e: FTP transmits credentials and data in clear text with no encryption by default.

q: An attacker tests a list of common passwords against an offline hash. What is the most specific name for this approach?
a: Dictionary attack
d: Exhaustive brute-force attack
Password spraying
Credential stuffing
e: A dictionary attack tests a wordlist. Exhaustive brute force enumerates a defined keyspace; spraying and stuffing describe online authentication strategies.
p: Different password attacks have different failure and lockout characteristics.

q: On Linux, what does 'ss -lntp' request?
a: Listening TCP sockets with addresses and process details
d: All UDP sockets and their DNS-resolved peers
Only established TCP sessions without process information
A capture of TCP payloads sent by every process
e: l selects listening sockets, n numeric output, t TCP, and p process information. Permissions can restrict process details. It is socket inspection, not packet capture.
p: Listing sockets is not capturing their traffic.

q: Which of the following IP addresses falls within a private range?
e: 192.168.1.1 lies in the RFC1918 private range 192.168.0.0/16.

q: Which of the following is an example of multifactor authentication?
a: Smart card and PIN
d: Password and password hint
Username and password
Fingerprint only
Security questions
e: A smart card (something you have) plus a PIN (something you know) combines two different factor types, true MFA.

q: If, during an authorised penetration test, you discover evidence of an intrusion on the target, which of the following would be the most appropriate course of action for the team?
a: Halt all test activities and contact the customer.
d: Continue the test and document the evidence.
Report to the local law enforcement immediately.
Attempt to trace the attacker.
Ignore the evidence and proceed as planned.
e: Stop all testing and contact the customer, continuing could destroy evidence or disrupt a live incident.

q: Which design best helps detect local log tampering after a server compromise?
a: A separately controlled append-only log collector
d: Encrypt logs with a key stored beside the logs
Store a second log copy on the same writable disk
Allow only the compromised root account to rotate logs
e: A separately controlled protected copy provides independent evidence. Encryption protects confidentiality; copies under the same compromised authority can both be changed.
p: Independent control of evidence matters more than a second filename.

q: On NTFS, what does 'type nc.exe > sol.exe:nc.exe' attempt?
a: Write bytes into a named alternate data stream on sol.exe
d: Rename nc.exe to sol.exe
Encrypt nc.exe using sol.exe as a key
Set a registry value under sol.exe
e: The colon identifies a named NTFS stream. This does not encrypt the bytes or create a network socket. Some tools omit streams in ordinary directory listings.
p: Alternate stream syntax is a filesystem operation.

q: At which layer of the OSI model is 'IPv4' considered to be?
a: Layer 3 (Network Layer)
d: Layer 1 (Physical Layer)
Layer 2 (Data Link Layer)
Layer 4 (Transport Layer)
Layer 5 (Session Layer)
e: IPv4 lives at the Network layer (Layer 3).

q: An IP address plus transport port identifies what in common networking terminology?
a: A transport endpoint
d: A complete bidirectional connection by itself
A DNS zone
An Ethernet broadcast domain
e: A connection normally needs both endpoints and the protocol, commonly expressed as a five-tuple. A single address/port pair is one endpoint.
p: One endpoint is not a whole connection.

q: How did a classic Ping of Death attack differ from an ordinary ping flood?
a: It abused reassembly of malformed oversized IP datagrams
d: It exhausted capacity with valid small echo requests
It filled a TCP backlog using half-open sessions
It redirected replies through poisoned ARP entries
e: The historical attack triggered reassembly bugs. A ping flood consumes resources by volume, a SYN flood targets TCP state, and ARP poisoning changes neighbor mappings.
p: Malformed-packet exploitation and traffic-volume exhaustion are different mechanisms.

q: What is the purpose of the ICMP protocol?
a: It takes care of error-handling in the network
d: It manages data encryption
It controls the flow of email traffic
It establishes TCP connections
It manages DNS resolutions
e: ICMP handles error and control messaging within IP networks.

q: Which of the following corresponds to the IPv6 loopback address?
d: ::FFFF
e: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address, the equivalent of 127.0.0.1.

q: Because of a recent penetration test, you have been asked to recommend a new firewall for a rapidly expanding company. You have been asked what type of firewall would be best for the organization if used in conjunction with other products and only needs the capability to statelessly filter traffic by port or IP address?
a: An access control list implemented on a router
d: A stateful packet inspection firewall
A web application firewall
An intrusion detection system
A reverse proxy
e: An access control list on a router provides the packet-filtering firewall function asked for here.

q: Of the following choices, what best describes a method of managing the flow of network traffic by allowing or denying traffic based on ports, protocols, and addresses?
a: Firewall rules
d: Proxy settings
Network segmentation
Virtual LANs
Load balancing
e: Firewall rules manage traffic flow by allowing or denying packets.

q: Which cipher was selected by NIST as the basis of AES?
a: Rijndael
d: Serpent
Twofish
RC6
e: Rijndael was selected; AES standardizes a 128-bit block and three key lengths. The other choices were AES competition finalists.
p: The broader Rijndael family is not identical to every AES parameter choice.

q: What does preimage resistance mean for a cryptographic hash?
a: Finding an input for a given digest should be computationally difficult
d: Different inputs must never share any output
The digest can be decrypted using the original salt
Every short password is impossible to guess offline
e: A finite digest space necessarily has collisions. Preimage resistance is a computational property; a small predictable password space can still be searched.
p: One-way hashing does not eliminate guessing.

q: Two parties share an HMAC key. What does a valid HMAC demonstrate to the receiver?
a: Integrity and shared-key message authentication
d: Confidentiality and proof that only the sender could create it
Publicly verifiable non-repudiation of the sender
Agreement of a fresh encryption key
e: An HMAC authenticates to key holders and detects modification. Both parties can generate it, so it is not a public signature or proof against the receiver. It does not encrypt.
p: Shared-key authentication is not non-repudiation.

q: Which of the following algorithms cannot be used for reversible encryption?
a: SHA-256
d: Blowfish
AES
RC4
RSA
e: SHA-256 is a one-way hash and cannot be reversed (decrypted), unlike an encryption cipher.

q: Which of the following best describes Tripwire?
a: It is used to verify integrity
d: It is an encryption tool
It is a firewall software
It is a network scanner
It is an anti-virus solution
e: Tripwire is a file-integrity checker that detects unauthorised changes to files.

q: A tool hashes only a file's content bytes. Which change leaves its digest unchanged, assuming the bytes remain identical?
a: Renaming the file
d: Adding a newline to the file
Changing one byte in the file
Appending a space to the file
e: A content hash does not include a pathname or permission metadata unless the tool explicitly incorporates them. Byte changes normally change a cryptographic digest.
p: Know what is actually included in the hash input.

q: Two identical passwords use distinct random salts with the same password-hashing scheme. What is the main expected benefit?
a: Reduced reuse of precomputed guesses across accounts
d: The salts must remain secret for verification to work
Offline guesses become impossible for either account
The salt substitutes for a slow work factor
e: Distinct salts produce distinct stored hashes and defeat broad precomputation reuse. An attacker can still guess per account; use a costly password-hashing scheme too.
p: A salt is public uniqueness, not an extra secret password.

q: A downloaded file and a checksum come from the same untrusted server. What does a matching checksum prove?
a: Agreement with the supplied checksum only
d: The file is safe because its bytes match a digest
The server's identity has been independently verified
The file was signed by a trusted publisher
e: An attacker controlling both artifacts can replace both. Authenticate the checksum or verify a trusted signature to obtain an origin guarantee.
p: Integrity against accidental change is not authenticated provenance.

q: How many secret bits in a 128-bit WEP key?
e: A 128-bit WEP key is 104 secret bits plus the 24-bit IV.

q: Alice wants to send Bob an encrypted message that only Bob can decrypt. Which key is used in a conventional public-key encryption design?
a: Bob's public key for encryption
d: Alice's private key for encryption
Alice's public key for encryption
Bob's private key for encryption
e: Bob decrypts with his private key. Signing with Alice's private key is a different operation; modern systems often use hybrid encryption for the payload.
p: Encryption recipient and signature author play different roles.

q: Which relationship between WPA and WPA2 is historically accurate?
a: WPA was interim; WPA2 implements full 802.11i
d: WPA2 replaced AES with RC4 to support older hardware
WPA introduced CCMP as the mandatory interoperable cipher
WPA2 removed enterprise authentication and retained only PSK
e: WPA provided an interim upgrade using TKIP; WPA2 certification followed the full 802.11i framework with CCMP support. Exact capabilities still depend on configuration.
p: Do not equate the interim WPA program with full WPA2 requirements.

q: Why was TKIP introduced for existing WEP-era hardware?
a: RC4 improvements compatible with existing hardware
d: To replace RC4 with AES on all existing adapters
To encrypt management frames without changing data protection
To use a single static IV for every packet in a session
e: TKIP retained RC4 for compatibility while improving per-packet key mixing and adding a MIC. It remains legacy and should not be selected for new deployments.
p: Interim compatibility is not modern security.

q: An attacker and victim are already in the same VLAN. Which control most directly validates ARP bindings on the switch?
a: Dynamic ARP Inspection with trusted binding data
d: Placing the default gateway in another VLAN
Disabling DNS recursion on the resolver
Changing the SSID of an unrelated access point
e: Dynamic ARP Inspection checks ARP messages against bindings such as those learned by DHCP snooping. VLAN separation limits scope but does not authenticate ARP within one VLAN.
p: Segmentation alone does not stop same-segment spoofing.

q: What can remove a server as a single point of failure?
a: Clustering
d: VLAN tagging
WEP encryption
NAT translation
SNMP polling
e: Clustering removes a single server as a point of failure by providing redundancy and failover.

q: Which of the following can be used to lure attackers away from real servers and allow for their detection?
a: Honeypots
d: Firewalls
Proxy servers
IDS
VPNs
e: Honeypots lure attackers onto decoy systems so their activity can be detected and studied.

q: An ACK scan returns a RST from TCP/443. What is the appropriate Nmap interpretation?
a: Unfiltered; listening state remains unknown
d: Open; an application has completed a handshake
Closed; no application can be listening there
Filtered; the RST proves a stateful firewall blocked it
e: ACK scans map filtering behavior. A RST means the probe reached a responding stack or device; both open and closed ports may respond.
p: An ACK probe is not a SYN probe.

q: An idle scan makes use of which of the following parameters?
a: The IPID
d: TTL values
ICMP Echo Replies
ACK responses
Port numbers
e: An idle (zombie) scan relies on the predictable IPID of a third-party idle host to scan anonymously.

q: A UDP probe receives ICMPv4 Destination Unreachable, code 3. How does Nmap normally classify the port?
a: Closed
d: Filtered
Open
Unfiltered
e: Code 3 is Port Unreachable and normally means closed for a UDP scan. Other unreachable codes can mean filtered; no reply is open-or-filtered.
p: An unreachable message must be interpreted with its code and probe type.

q: A UDP scan reports open-or-filtered after no replies. Which conclusion is supported?
a: Open-or-filtered remains unresolved
d: An application was confirmed listening
The host was confirmed unreachable
A firewall was confirmed absent
e: Silence is ambiguous for UDP and some other scans. A protocol-aware probe may resolve it; silence alone is not positive service evidence.
p: Absence of a response is not absence of a service.

q: What does it mean if traceroute output includes a time annotation of !X, as in the following extract from traceroute output? traceroute to www.cleflab.eds.com (10.10.10.10), 30 hops max, 38 byte packets 1 Somerouter (192.168. 0.1) 1.246 ms 1.075 ms 1.002 ms 2 someotherrouter.eds.com (192.168.1.1) 1368.882 ms !X * *?
a: Communication administratively prohibited
d: Host unreachable
Network unreachable
Request timed out
TTL expired
e: !X in traceroute means communication administratively prohibited, a filter is dropping the packet.

q: What is IANA's dynamic/private port-number range?
e: IANA defines the dynamic/private range as 49152-65535. An operating system's ephemeral allocation range may differ.
p: Registry ranges and an OS's selected ephemeral range are not identical concepts.

q: While looking over data gathered by one of your co-workers, you come across the following data: system.sysDescr.0 = OCTET STRING: “Sun SNMP Agent”, system.sysObjectID.0 = OBJECT IDENTIFIER: enterprises.42.2.1.1 system.sysUpTime.0 = Timeticks: (5660402) 15:43:24 system.sysContact.0 = OCTET STRING: “System administrator” system.sysName.0 = OCTET STRING: “unixserver” system.sysLocation.0 = OCTET STRING: “System admins office” system.sysServices.0 = INTEGER: 72 interfaces.ifNumber.0 = INTEGER: 2 interfaces.ifTable.ifEntry.ifIndex.1 = INTEGER: 1 interfaces.ifTable.ifEntry.ifIndex.2 = INTEGER: 2 What was used to obtain this output?
a: An SNMP walk
d: Nmap scan
Netstat command
Traceroute
Ping sweep
e: Output listing OID/MIB values indicates an SNMP walk was performed.

q: A SYN flood can be detected by which of the following?
a: A large number of SYN packets appearing on the network without corresponding ACK responses
d: An increase in ICMP echo requests
A sudden drop in network traffic
Repeated ARP requests
A high number of FIN packets
e: A SYN flood shows as many SYN packets with no matching ACKs, leaving half-open connections piling up.

q: The ability to capture a stream of data packets and then insert them back into the network as a valid message is known as which of the following?
a: Packet replay
d: Man-in-the-middle
IP spoofing
Session hijacking
Packet fragmentation
e: Capturing packets and re-injecting them as valid traffic is a packet replay attack.

q: This DoS tool is characterized by the fact that it sends packets with the same source and destination address. What is it called?
a: Land
d: Smurf
Teardrop
Ping of Death
Trinoo
e: The Land attack sends a packet whose source and destination address/port are identical, hanging vulnerable stacks.

q: In a classic Smurf attack, why can the victim receive many more replies than the attacker sends requests?
a: A spoofed victim address is used in requests to an answering broadcast network
d: A TCP retransmission doubles every reply indefinitely
A DNS resolver signs each packet multiple times
An ARP request is fragmented into thousands of IP packets
e: Hosts responding to a directed-broadcast ICMP echo request send their replies to the spoofed victim address. The mechanism is reflection and amplification.
p: Identify amplification and reflection separately from a direct flood.

q: What is the purpose of 'HEAD / HTTP/1.0' followed by a blank line on a TCP HTTP connection?
a: Response metadata without response content
d: Request the full resource with a header-only request body
Request only the first bytes of the resource's content
Request every virtual host configured at that address
e: HEAD uses GET-like response semantics while omitting response content. The response can disclose headers; it does not necessarily prove a particular server implementation.
p: A header probe is useful evidence, not a definitive software attestation.

q: Which of the following is not a valid RIR (Regional Internet Registry)?
a: AFNIC
d: ARIN
APNIC
RIPE NCC
LACNIC
e: AFNIC is France's national domain registry, not a Regional Internet Registry; the RIRs are ARIN, RIPE, APNIC, LACNIC and AFRINIC.

q: In an SOA record, how is hostmaster.lab.net. conventionally interpreted in the responsible-mailbox field?
a: hostmaster@lab.net
d: A mail exchanger named hostmaster.lab.net
A zone named hostmaster with server lab.net
The DNSSEC public signing key
e: The first unescaped dot separates the local part and domain in this representation. The field identifies a responsible mailbox rather than an MX target.
p: SOA mailbox encoding differs from an ordinary hostname.

q: In SOA 'ns.example.test. hostmaster.example.test. 2026101401 3600 600 86400 300', which value is the serial?
e: The first numeric SOA field after server and mailbox is the serial. The following values are refresh, retry, expire, and minimum.
p: Read field position rather than guessing from a large number.

q: What does the DNS SOA record type stand for?
a: Start of Authority
d: System of Authentication
Source of Authority
Security of Access
State of Application
e: SOA stands for Start of Authority, the record holding a zone's authoritative metadata.

q: What is a DNS zone?
a: An administratively served portion of the DNS namespace
d: Every name beneath a domain regardless of delegation
A TCP connection to an authoritative server
A resolver's list of cached client queries
e: Delegation can split a domain subtree into separately administered zones. A zone and a domain are related, but not interchangeable.
p: Subdomains can lie in different zones.

q: An attacker poisons a cached positive A record. What most directly bounds how long that cached entry remains usable without refresh?
a: The positive record's remaining TTL
d: The zone's SOA refresh interval
The zone's SOA retry interval
The authoritative server's TCP timeout
e: Positive records have their own TTLs. SOA values are relevant to zone maintenance and negative caching, not a universal lifetime for all cached answers.
p: Positive and negative caching use different rules.

q: A Cisco SNMP copy row sets source to networkFile and destination to startupConfig. What direction is intended?
a: Transfer a network file into the device's startup configuration
d: Transfer the running configuration into the caller's browser
Copy every interface counter into the DNS resolver
Remove the saved configuration without retrieving any file
e: Interpret source, destination, transport, and server fields together. A write-capable community may make this an impactful operation.
p: File-copy direction follows the configured endpoints.

q: Why should a tester inspect the TFTP server address in an SNMP configuration-copy request?
a: It identifies the external endpoint used for the copy
d: It authenticates the request's human operator
It determines the router's entire IP routing table
It encrypts the copied configuration automatically
e: The address binds the management action to a transfer endpoint. Network reachability and file permissions remain additional conditions.
p: An address in a request is not necessarily the device being tested.

q: In Cisco's configuration-copy MIB, what does a runningConfig source select?
a: The device's currently active configuration
d: Only the last saved startup configuration
Every user's workstation configuration
The network file named by the destination field
e: Running and startup configuration can differ. The source selector determines which state is exported.
p: Active and saved device state are not always identical.

q: What is a common confidentiality weakness of conventional SNMPv1/v2c?
a: Community strings and managed values can be visible on the wire
d: Every version encrypts only the community string
v2c requires a validated client certificate
SNMP encrypts the IP headers with its community string
e: Community-based SNMP lacks the USM auth/privacy levels introduced with SNMPv3. Restricting reachability reduces exposure but does not add encryption.
p: Specify the version and security model.

q: Which of the following uses a data structure, in the form of a tree, known as a Management Information Base (MIB)?
a: SNMP
d: FTP
DNS
HTTP
Telnet
e: SNMP organises managed data as a tree called the Management Information Base (MIB).

q: Which of the following is not a valid SIP method as defined by RFC 3261?
a: HANGUP
d: ACK
BYE
OPTIONS
CANCEL
e: HANGUP is not a valid SIP method; BYE is used to end a call.

q: Why can reconnecting a wireless client expose additional assessment evidence?
a: Association and authentication exchanges may become observable
d: Every reconnection reveals the plaintext passphrase
Reconnection guarantees administrator login to the AP
Every reconnected client must choose a new SSID
e: The useful evidence depends on authentication method and captured exchange. Disruption also needs appropriate test authorization.
p: An observable exchange is not a plaintext credential.

q: Which EAP method below lacks mutual server authentication by design?
a: EAP-MD5
d: EAP-TLS with validated certificates
PEAP with validated server certificate
EAP-TTLS with validated server certificate
e: EAP-MD5 provides a challenge-response check without server authentication. Certificate validation is essential to the server-authentication guarantee in tunneled methods.
p: Naming a certificate-based method is insufficient if validation is disabled.

q: Which of the following may be described as: part of the IEEE 802.11i standard, implements per-packet key mixing with a re-keying system and also provides a message integrity check?
a: TKIP
d: AES
WPA2
EAP
RC4
e: TKIP is the 802.11i component that does per-packet key mixing as an interim WEP fix.

q: You are hosting a wireless hotspot, and you want to segment wireless users from each other. What should you use?
a: Isolation mode
d: WPA2 encryption
RADIUS authentication
VPN tunneling
Channel hopping
e: Client isolation mode stops wireless users on the same hotspot from communicating with each other.

q: You have been asked to install and turn on WEP on an access point that is used in the shipping area. Which of the following statements is true?
a: The MAC addresses can still be sniffed
d: WEP is unbreakable when properly configured
SSID is always hidden when using WEP
WEP protects against MAC spoofing
WEP encrypts MAC addresses
e: Even with WEP enabled, MAC addresses travel in clear text and can be sniffed (then spoofed to defeat MAC filtering).

q: What is the maximum length of an IIEEE 802.11 SSID element?
a: 32 octets
d: 32 bits
64 octets
128 bits
e: The SSID has a maximum length of 32 octets, not 32 bits. Its interpretation and display depend on the byte sequence.
p: Bits and bytes differ by a factor of eight.

q: Why is MAC filtering a weak sole control against unauthorized Wi-Fi devices?
a: An observed address can often be imitated
d: A MAC address is cryptographically signed by a public CA
Filtering automatically encrypts all data frames
The address is hidden by every WPA2 deployment
e: Use suitable authentication and segmentation. Address filtering may aid administration but does not prove device identity.
p: Identifiers are not necessarily authenticators.

q: Why can changing a router's startup configuration leave current behavior apparently unchanged?
a: Saved startup state may not yet be applied to the running state
d: All saved changes are always ignored permanently
The router only accepts changes through DNS
The file necessarily becomes a user session cookie
e: Running and startup state have different lifecycles. Verify both actual current state and behavior after any agreed reload.
p: Immediate behavior does not describe every persisted change.

q: Why protect an exported router configuration as sensitive evidence?
a: It may contain reusable credentials and internal topology
d: It consists only of public Ethernet standards
It can never identify other systems
It is encrypted by TFTP automatically
e: Configuration contents can expose secrets and architecture. Inspect actual material and apply appropriate evidence handling.
p: A configuration file can connect several otherwise separate risks.

q: Which description best fits LDAP?
a: A protocol for querying and modifying directory entries
d: A cipher for encrypting Windows password databases
A transport for distributing Group Policy files over SMB
A ticket format issued by the Kerberos KDC
e: LDAP accesses directories; Active Directory uses it alongside DNS, Kerberos, and SMB. LDAP is not itself a Windows password cipher or ticket.
p: Directory access and authentication are related but distinct.

q: Which Windows command displays group SIDs and attributes for the current access token?
a: whoami /groups
d: net user /domain
gpresult /r
dsquery user
netstat -a
e: whoami /groups shows the current user's group memberships, account type and SIDs.

q: Which ticket-based protocol is commonly used for authentication in an Active Directory domain?
a: Kerberos
d: RADIUS
TACACS+
LDAP
OAuth
e: Active Directory uses Kerberos as its primary authentication protocol.

q: On Windows, what does setting the Account Lockout Threshold to 0 mean?
a: The account will never be locked out (lockout is disabled)
d: The account locks after one failed attempt
The account is locked permanently
Lockout applies only to the Administrator
e: A threshold of 0 disables lockout entirely, so password guessing is unconstrained. A non-zero value sets how many failed attempts trigger a lockout; note the built-in Administrator (RID 500) is exempt regardless.

q: An account named Helpdesk has a SID ending -500. What does the RID identify?
a: The built-in Administrator account for that authority
d: An arbitrary user with an administrator-looking name
The built-in Guest account
The first domain computer account
e: RID 500 persists when the built-in Administrator is renamed. Check the authority and actual token rather than relying on the name.
p: Stable identifiers can matter more than display labels.

q: Which statement is accurate about stored LM and NT password hashes?
a: Neither uses a per-account random salt
d: Only NT uses a per-account random salt
Only LM uses a per-account random salt
Both use the account SID as a random salt
e: Stored LM/NT hashes are unsalted. NTLMv1/v2 challenge-response exchanges are different artifacts with additional protocol inputs; do not conflate them.
p: Stored hashes and network challenge-responses are not the same format.

q: How do Windows cached domain-logon verifiers differ from a raw NT hash?
a: A distinct cached verifier incorporating the username
d: They are always a plaintext copy of the password
They are reusable NTLM network responses for every challenge
They are the same format as a Kerberos service ticket
e: DCC/MSCache verifiers support cached logon checks and offline guessing. A DCC value is not simply the NT hash used in standard pass-the-hash.
p: Identify the exact credential artifact before inferring reuse.

q: The second half of an LM hash is AAD3B435B51404EE. What does this usually suggest for a valid LM hash?
a: The second seven-byte half of the password input was empty
d: The original password had exactly fourteen characters
The original password was necessarily all lowercase
The password was stored using a unique random salt
e: LM processes two seven-byte halves independently. An empty second half suggests no input beyond the first seven bytes. It does not reveal case because LM uppercases input.
p: The LM half length is seven bytes, not eight characters.

q: On host A, xterm -display B:0.0 launches successfully. Where does the process run and where does its window appear?
a: The process runs on A and displays on B
d: The process runs on B and displays on A
Both process and display run on A
Both process and display run on B
e: The command starts a local X client. -display chooses the X server that draws its window; it does not move process execution to that server.
p: X clients and X servers reverse a common desktop intuition.

q: What is the correct sequence to send SMTP mail?
a: HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA.
d: EHLO, RCPT TO, MAIL FROM, DATA
MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, HELO, DATA
DATA, HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO
RCPT TO, MAIL FROM, DATA, HELO
e: The SMTP send sequence is HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, then DATA.

q: What is the significant difference between 'xhost +172.16.5.13' and 'xhost +'?
a: One host allowed versus broad access-control removal
d: The first enables encryption; the second disables encryption
The first launches a remote shell; the second launches a local shell
Both restrict access to 172.16.5.13
e: The bare plus opens access broadly. A specific host addition is narrower, though X11 trust and transport configuration still matter. Neither enables encryption.
p: A missing address can change the security effect dramatically.

q: Which of the following ports is used for the XDMCP service?
a: UDP 177
d: TCP 23
UDP 69
TCP 515
UDP 514
e: XDMCP (the X Display Manager Control Protocol) uses UDP port 177.

q: Why should old IIS extension paths matter during an assessment of a legacy server?
a: An exposed extension may add its own vulnerable request handler
d: Every extension grants anonymous SYSTEM access
Extensions replace all application authorization checks
IIS extensions can only process encrypted inputs
e: Legacy handlers have their own code and configuration. Confirm exact applicability rather than inferring compromise from a path.
p: An installed component and an exploitable instance are different facts.

q: After application-level command execution, what primarily determines the command's OS privileges?
a: The worker or service execution identity and controls
d: The application's marketing name
The visitor's browser version
The public HTTP port number
e: A server product/version alone does not establish SYSTEM, root, or an anonymous account context. Verify identity and isolation.
p: Do not infer execution privilege from the server brand.

q: You noticed the following entry: http://server/cgi-bin/phf?Qalias=x%0a/bin/cat%20/etc/passwd What is the attacker attempting to do?
a: Exploit a vulnerability in a CGI script
d: Initiate a SQL injection attack
Attempt a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack
Execute a buffer overflow
Perform a Directory Traversal
e: The %0a injects a newline so the vulnerable phf CGI runs /bin/cat /etc/passwd, exploiting a CGI flaw.

q: In classic RADIUS without a secure outer transport, which statement is accurate?
a: The User-Password attribute is hidden; the full packet is not encrypted
d: The entire packet is protected like a TLS record
All attributes are encrypted using the server's public key
Only the packet header is encrypted
e: Classic RADIUS hides User-Password using the shared secret and request authenticator; other attributes can remain visible. RADIUS over TLS is a different deployment.
p: Protecting one attribute is not encrypting all traffic.

q: What is RADIUS?
a: Remote Authentication Dial In User Service
d: Routing and Distance Information Under Service
Regional Address Database in User Systems
Remote Access Dial-up Interface User Service
Remote Authentication Database Information User Service
e: RADIUS stands for Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service, a centralised AAA protocol.

q: A response sets an unfamiliar load-balancer-looking cookie. What can this initially support?
a: A hypothesis about routing or infrastructure behavior
d: Proof of a particular exploitable vendor version
Proof that the application has no authentication
Proof that the cookie is a plaintext password
e: Cookies can reveal routing conventions and persistence. Names and values may be customized, so correlate actual behavior.
p: Fingerprint artifacts need corroboration.

q: What does the HTTP response code 307 mean?
a: Temporary Redirect
d: Permanent Redirect
Found
Not Modified
See Other
e: HTTP 307 is a Temporary Redirect that, unlike 302, preserves the original request method (e.g. a POST stays a POST). 308 is the permanent equivalent.

q: Which condition is described by HTTP 413 in current HTTP semantics?
a: Content Too Large
d: URI Too Long
Unsupported Media Type
Length Required
e: 413 concerns request content size. 414 concerns the URI, 415 media type, and 411 a required content length. Older texts use 'Request Entity Too Large'.
p: Historical reason phrases can change while the status meaning persists.

q: Which of the following describes the HTTP status code 407?
a: Proxy Authentication Required
d: Unauthorized
Forbidden
Payment Required
Conflict
e: HTTP 407 means Proxy Authentication Required.

q: Which port does HTTPS use?
e: HTTPS uses TCP 443.

q: Which of the following is the correct definition of NASL?
a: NASL is a scripting language designed for the Nessus security scanner.
d: NASL is a network-attached storage language.
NASL is a protocol used for network security.
NASL is a file transfer protocol.
NASL is a scripting language for Snort.
e: NASL is the Nessus Attack Scripting Language, used to write Nessus vulnerability checks.

q: Which activity is passive relative to the target's systems?
a: Reading a third-party registry's published record
d: Requesting the target's robots.txt directly
Attempting an AXFR against the target nameserver
Crawling every page on the target server
e: Third-party published data avoids direct contact with the target service. That does not guarantee secrecy from every observer.
p: Passive describes the collection relationship, not invisibility.

q: While searching a website, you have been unable to find information that was on the site several months ago. What might you do to attempt to locate that information?
a: Use the wayback machine
d: Check the DNS records
Use a web crawler
Contact the webmaster
Access the server logs
e: The Wayback Machine (web archive) can recover content that was removed from the live site.

q: What is a benefit of making an authorized local copy of public site content?
a: Repeatable offline review of the captured material
d: A guarantee that every authenticated route was captured
Automatic access to the backend database
A guarantee that the content remains current
e: A snapshot supports review and comparison but has capture-time and coverage limits. Authenticated and dynamic behavior may require separate collection.
p: A mirror is a snapshot, not a complete application model.

q: A UNION query requests banner from Oracle's v$version. What is the tester seeking?
a: Database version information
d: The operating-system password file
The browser's session storage
A wireless network's SSID
e: v$version exposes Oracle version-related information when accessible. UNION shape and account privileges still constrain the attempt.
p: A known metadata target does not guarantee access.

q: Two distinct input messages have the same digest under one hash function. What is this called?
a: A hash collision
d: A preimage by definition
A digital signature
A key exchange
e: A collision requires different inputs with equal outputs. Preimage problems start from a specified digest and seek an input; a signature is a separate construction.
p: State which objects are different and which values match.

q: A quote in a parameter triggers a database syntax error. What is the strongest supported conclusion before further testing?
a: A SQL-parsing signal needing confirmation
d: SQL injection with full database control is established
The backend is definitely Microsoft SQL Server
Operating-system command execution is established
e: An error is a lead, not proof of the entire impact chain. Controlled boolean or timing comparisons can establish influence. Driver errors do not necessarily identify the database or privileges.
p: Distinguish a diagnostic signal from validated exploitation.

q: The following request to an IIS webserver is an example of what kind of attack? http://www.example.com/scripts/..%255c../winnt/system32/attrib.exe?c:\*.*?
a: IIS Unicode double decode directory traversal
d: SQL Injection
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Buffer Overflow
Command Injection
e: %255c double-decodes to a backslash, escaping the web root, this is the IIS Unicode directory-traversal bug.

q: A requested path contains ..%255c..%255c. What transformation is the tester probing?
a: Multiple decoding into parent-directory separators
d: RSA public-key encryption of a session cookie
DNS compression of a mail-server hostname
TCP reassembly of a fragmented TLS record
e: %25 decodes to a percent sign; a subsequent pass can decode %5c to backslash. Whether traversal succeeds depends on the application and filesystem.
p: Track each decoding pass and the platform's separators.

q: Which SQL Server feature can run operating-system commands when enabled and permitted?
a: xp_cmdshell
d: sp_who
sp_helptext
SELECT DB_NAME()
e: xp_cmdshell crosses into OS command execution under a configured account. The other choices provide database/session information.
p: Command execution depends on enablement, caller rights, and execution identity.

q: Why are historical Oracle default credentials worth recognizing during legacy assessments?
a: They suggest bounded, version-aware checks for unchanged installations
d: They prove all modern installations share the same password
They establish remote SYSDBA access on every listener
They remove the need to verify account lockout behavior
e: Historical knowledge helps form hypotheses. Installer behavior, account state, version, and current credentials still need validation.
p: Historical defaults are not universal current facts.

q: Which pair is conventionally recognized as a historical Oracle demonstration account?
a: SCOTT / TIGER
d: sa / guest
root / toor
postgres / postgres
e: SCOTT/TIGER is associated with sample schemas in older material. Availability and authentication depend on installation and configuration.
p: A sample account is not necessarily present or enabled.

q: Which distinction best separates a classic worm from a classic file-infecting virus?
a: Worm: independent propagation; virus: host-code infection
d: A worm replicates; a virus cannot replicate
A virus spreads over networks; a worm never does
A worm needs a host executable; a virus never does
e: Both can replicate. The distinction concerns dependence on host code and propagation mechanisms, not whether replication exists.
p: Avoid the false statement that viruses are not self-replicating.

q: What is the intended purpose of Windows kernel patch protection on supported x64 systems?
a: Detect prohibited changes to certain kernel structures
d: Encrypt every user's NT password hash
Sign every HTTP response automatically
Replace all application privilege checks
e: Kernel patch protection and protected-process mechanisms are distinct safeguards. Neither is a universal defense against all exploitation.
p: Separate kernel-integrity controls from process-access controls.

q: The art of hiding information in graphics or music files is known as which of the following?
a: Steganography
d: Cryptography
Encoding
Hashing
Watermarking
e: Hiding information inside images or audio files is steganography.

q: With a standard 1500-byte Ethernet payload and 8 bytes of PPPoE/PPP overhead, what IP MTU is conventionally available?
a: 1492 bytes
d: 1500 bytes
1480 bytes
1518 bytes
e: 1500-8=1492. Extensions with larger Ethernet payloads can support other values; the stated premise determines the answer.
p: MTU arithmetic needs an explicit encapsulation assumption.

q: What is IMAP primarily used for?
a: Storing and retrieving emails
d: Sending emails
Encrypting emails
Filtering spam
Archiving emails
e: IMAP stores and retrieves email on the server, unlike POP3 which typically downloads and deletes it.

q: Alice wants confidential email to Bob with a verifiable signature from Alice. Which key roles are correct?
a: Alice's private signing key; Bob's public encryption key
d: Sign with Bob's public key; encrypt for Alice's private key
Sign with Alice's public key; encrypt for Bob's private key
Sign with Bob's private key; encrypt for Alice's public key
e: Bob verifies using Alice's public key and decrypts using his own private key. Real email encryption typically uses a symmetric content key wrapped for the recipient.
p: Keep signing and recipient-encryption key roles separate.

q: Your organization is considering deploying multiple servers using a standardized image. Of the following choices, what best describes the security benefit of this plan?
a: The image can include mandated security configurations
d: It reduces network latency
Increases disk space availability
Provides faster data backup
Simplifies licensing compliance
e: A standardised image lets you bake mandated security configurations into every server consistently.

q: A victim believes they are clicking a visible button, but an overlaid frame sends the click to another site's sensitive action. What is this?
a: Clickjacking
d: Session fixation
Reflected XSS
DNS rebinding
e: Clickjacking deceives the user through UI framing. It does not require script execution in the target's origin. Frame restrictions mitigate it.
p: A malicious click target is not necessarily an XSS payload.

q: Which of these is a valid Email header field?
a: Return-Path
d: From-Name
Email-Host
Sender-Info
Reply-Address
e: Return-Path is a valid email header (it holds the bounce/return address).

q: Which element conventionally marks footer content in HTML5?
a: <footer>
d: <blink>
<frameset>
<applet>
e: HTML5 added semantic elements such as footer. Semantic structure does not itself enforce application access controls.
p: Markup meaning and security enforcement are separate.

q: Which of the following is not a commonly-used web server?
a: FreeBSD
d: Apache
Nginx
IIS
Tomcat
e: FreeBSD is an operating system, not a web server; Apache, IIS and nginx are web servers.

q: Which statement regarding a pentest report is true?
a: The technical details will be read by the IT/Information security people responsible.
d: The pentest report should not contain recommendations.
The pentest report is only for the company's management.
It should always be written in non-technical language.
It must be kept confidential from the client.
e: The technical detail section is read by the IT and security staff responsible for remediation.

q: Untrusted input is interpreted as shell syntax rather than one data argument. Which issue is most specific?
a: OS command injection
d: SQL injection
Cross-site request forgery
Directory-listing disclosure
e: The interpreter receiving the input determines the injection class. Shell escaping or avoiding a shell matters; SQL parameters address a different sink.
p: Name the interpreter that crosses the data/code boundary.

q: Which description best fits an 802.11 beacon frame?
a: Periodic AP management advertisement
d: A data frame carrying encrypted user application bytes
A control frame acknowledging one successfully received data frame
A probe request sent only by a station looking for a network
e: Beacons advertise network parameters and timing. Probe requests come from stations; acknowledgments and data frames have different roles.
p: A beacon may help measure signal strength, but that is not its definition.

q: Which pair describes TKIP's underlying cipher and its Michael integrity check?
a: RC4 and a 64-bit MIC
d: AES and a 128-bit GCM tag
DES and a 32-bit CRC
RC4 and a 256-bit SHA-2 signature
e: TKIP retains RC4 and adds the Michael MIC plus key mixing. A MIC is not a public-key signature; TKIP's design is now legacy.
p: Do not confuse cipher, checksum, MAC, and signature.

q: What does net localgroup display when no group name or modification switch is supplied?
a: View all local groups
d: List all network shares
Check active network connections
Display all domain users
Show all running processes
e: net localgroup lists all local groups on the host.

q: What does net localgroup GROUPNAME display when no modification switch is supplied?
a: View info about a specific group
d: Delete the specified group
Change the group's permissions
Create a new group
Add a new member to the group
e: net localgroup [group] shows the members and details of a specific local group.

q: What does net share display when no modification arguments are supplied?
a: Look at shares locally
d: Connect to remote shares
Remove all shared folders
Create a new network share
List all network connections
e: net share lists the shares offered by the local host.

q: A legacy 'net view' browse list contains five computers. What can you safely conclude?
a: A partial browse-list observation
d: The domain has exactly five computer accounts
Only those five hosts have any reachable services
Every returned host is a domain controller
e: Browse-list discovery is not an exhaustive inventory. Availability, discovery protocols, and membership can make its view incomplete.
p: A discovery list is a view, not proof of completeness.

q: What does legacy 'net view /domain' request when browse services are available?
a: A list of available domain or workgroup names
d: All Group Policy objects in the current domain
All users in every trusted domain
All domain controller password hashes
e: The command lists browse-domain/workgroup names, not all information about a domain. LDAP and other interfaces serve different enumeration purposes.
p: A command's broad-sounding name does not define its actual output.

q: What does 'net user USERNAME /domain' normally request?
a: Details of the named domain user, including relevant memberships
d: Creation of the named local user
Deletion of the named domain user
Every domain user's password hash
e: The command queries the user when no creation/deletion switches are supplied. Its output is account information, not a credential dump.
p: Distinguish an account query from a modifying command.

q: Which statement best describes the SYSVOL share on a domain controller?
a: Replicated domain policy files and scripts
d: It stores the live ntds.dit password database for anonymous download
It exposes each workstation's local SAM database
It is a private temporary share used only by the SQL service
e: SYSVOL includes Group Policy files and scripts. Its read access is expected for clients; writable policy or exposed secrets are different concerns.
p: Readable policy files are not the same as readable directory password hashes.

q: What does the NETLOGON share normally expose on a domain controller?
a: The domain logon-script directory within SYSVOL
d: The complete Windows Security event log
The Kerberos ticket database
The entire Group Policy tree as a separate database
e: NETLOGON typically maps to SYSVOL's scripts directory. Group Policy files are located elsewhere within SYSVOL; neither share is a direct password database.
p: Do not equate the share name with audit logs or all policy data.

q: What is NNTP used for?
a: Transferring and accessing network news articles
d: Issuing DNS authoritative responses
Transferring SSH host keys
Resolving Ethernet neighbor addresses
e: NNTP supports article transfer and access to newsgroups. Public archives can expose historical technical information about organizations.
p: News infrastructure can be an information source without being a test target.

q: What can you use SNMP for?
a: To enumerate network, host info, and OS info
d: Transfer arbitrary files using the FTP PORT command
Retrieve every user password hash through Kerberos
Decrypt HTTPS payloads using the community string
e: SNMP can be used to enumerate network, host and OS information from managed devices.

q: A rogue DHCP server offers clients an attacker-controlled gateway and DNS server. What risk does this create?
a: Traffic redirection and possible interception
d: Automatic decryption of every TLS session
Guaranteed remote code execution on every client
A requirement to abandon IPv4 immediately
e: Clients accepting rogue network configuration may route or resolve through the attacker. TLS validation and other controls may still protect higher-layer traffic.
p: A network interception position is not automatic application compromise.

q: What is the purpose of a DHCP starvation attack?
a: Consume available DHCP leases with many client identities
d: Redirecting DHCP traffic to another server for packet sniffing.
Resetting the DHCP lease time to zero, forcing re-authentication.
Spoofing IP addresses to bypass firewall rules.
Creating a fake DHCP pool to intercept traffic.
e: A starvation attack attempts to exhaust the address pool, denying leases to legitimate clients. It does not itself prove that a rogue server will subsequently succeed.

q: Which conventional port pair is associated with SIP signaling and SIP over TLS?
a: 5060 TCP/UDP and 5061 TCP
d: 5060 UDP and 5061 UDP only
500 UDP and 4500 UDP
1723 TCP and IP protocol 47
e: SIP conventionally uses 5060 over UDP or TCP and 5061 over TCP for TLS. RTP media uses separately negotiated ports.
p: SIP signaling ports do not describe the media path.

q: A SIP server returns '100 Trying' to an INVITE. What does this mean?
a: The request is being processed
d: The called party is definitely ringing
The call was accepted and media is flowing
The user was permanently moved
e: 100 is provisional processing feedback. 180 indicates ringing and 200 is a successful final response; neither proves media quality by itself.
p: Provisional signaling is not completed call establishment.

q: What does SIP 180 Ringing indicate?
a: Callee is ringing
d: Callee is on hold
Server is busy
Authentication in progress
Session timed out
e: SIP 180 (Ringing) means the callee's phone is ringing.

q: What does SIP 181 Call Is Being Forwarded indicate?
a: Call is being forwarded
d: Call rejected by callee
Server initiating a new session
Callee is unavailable
Session encrypted
e: SIP 181 means the call is being forwarded.

q: What does a SIP 200 response indicate for the request it answers?
a: Request is successful
d: Request timeout
Session not established
Server unavailable
Request denied
e: SIP 200 (OK) means the request succeeded.

q: A SIP server returns 404 Not Found for a request. What does that response indicate?
a: The request's user or domain was not found at that server
d: The caller's credentials are necessarily invalid
The callee is definitely busy
The server has negotiated encrypted media
e: 404 reports an unrecognized target at the responding server. 401/407 concern authentication and 486 concerns busy signaling.
p: A SIP response refers to a particular request and server context.

q: What does /boot commonly contain on a traditional Linux layout?
a: Linux kernel and other files needed by the boot managers.
d: User configuration files and system logs
System binaries and essential drivers
Temporary files created during boot
Hardware device drivers and firmware
e: /boot holds the Linux kernel and the files the boot loader needs.

q: What does /dev primarily expose on Linux?
a: Device nodes and related interfaces
d: Contains system configuration files
Holds user data and documents
Stores log files and error reports
Contains essential boot scripts
e: /dev contains device files that represent hardware.

q: What does /etc primarily contain on Linux?
a: Contains system configuration files and initialization scripts
d: Holds device drivers and firmware
Stores temporary system data
Contains user application binaries
Hosts multimedia files and libraries
e: /etc holds system configuration files and initialisation scripts.

q: After filesystem recovery, what is an ext-family filesystem's lost+found directory commonly used for?
a: Reconnected orphaned files or directories found by repair
d: Every file deleted by users during normal operation
All files that lack execute permissions
Files whose owner has logged out
e: A filesystem checker can reconnect orphaned inodes into lost+found. It is not a universal recycle bin or a list of ownerless permissions.
p: Filesystem recovery is different from ordinary undelete behavior.

q: What is /media conventionally used for on a Linux filesystem layout?
a: Mount points for removable media
d: Stores system log files
Contains user application binaries
Holds device driver installations
Houses system configuration backups
e: /media is where removable media such as USB drives and CDs are mounted.

q: What is /mnt conventionally used for on a Linux filesystem layout?
a: A conventional mount point for temporary mounts
d: Contains system kernel files
Holds user authentication data
Stores permanent system binaries
Hosts virtual machine images
e: /mnt is a mount point for temporarily mounted filesystems.

q: What is /opt conventionally used for on a Linux filesystem layout?
a: Add-on application software packages
d: Contains core system libraries
Stores encrypted user data
Holds kernel-level configuration
Contains essential system drivers
e: /opt holds optional or third-party software packages.

q: What is /proc on a typical Linux system?
a: Virtual process and kernel information
d: A disk directory containing all installed binaries
A permanent archive of every process's deleted files
A mounted copy of the password database
e: procfs synthesizes information such as process details and kernel state; it is not a disk-backed archive. Access controls and mount options still matter.
p: A virtual filesystem is not a directory of ordinary saved files.

q: What does /sbin conventionally contain on a traditional Linux layout?
a: System administration binaries
d: Holds multimedia files
Stores user documents
Contains temporary internet files
Hosts shared libraries
e: /sbin holds system administration binaries.

q: What does /srv conventionally contain?
a: Site-specific data provided by system services
d: Holds user preferences
Contains encrypted backup files
Stores device driver installations
Hosts system error logs
e: /srv holds data served by the system, such as web and FTP content.

q: What does Linux sysfs at /sys expose?
a: Virtual device and kernel object information
d: Stores user data
Contains system logs
Hosts user applications
Holds temporary cache files
e: /sys exposes device and kernel information via sysfs.

q: What type of data is conventionally stored under /var?
a: Variable data such as logs, queues, and state
d: Stores device drivers
Hosts user applications
Contains kernel modules
Holds backup configurations
e: /var holds variable data such as logs, mail and spool files.

q: A Unix password field begins $5$salt$. Which scheme does this indicate?
a: SHA-256-crypt
d: Raw SHA-256 without a salt
SHA-1-crypt
bcrypt
e: $5$ identifies the salted SHA-256-crypt password scheme, not any arbitrary SHA-256 digest. Parameters such as rounds affect verification cost.
p: Format markers identify a scheme and parameters, not just digest length.

q: A Unix password field begins $6$salt$. Which scheme does this indicate?
a: SHA-512-crypt
d: Raw SHA-512 without a salt
MD5-crypt
bcrypt
e: $6$ identifies SHA-512-crypt. It is a salted password scheme; the marker should not be confused with a raw SHA-512 digest.
p: Underlying algorithms and stored password formats are different abstractions.

q: A stored password hash begins with $2a$. What scheme is indicated?
a: bcrypt
d: Raw Blowfish encryption
MD5-crypt
SHA-512-crypt
e: $2a$ is a bcrypt marker. bcrypt uses a Blowfish-derived construction but is a password-hashing scheme, not reversible Blowfish ciphertext.
p: Name the storage scheme rather than only its building block.

q: Which SMTP commands may provide user-enumeration signals when a server's responses disclose mailbox validity?
a: VRFY, EXPN, and RCPT TO
d: RETR, DELE, and STAT
LIST, GET, and PUT
SELECT, FETCH, and STORE
e: VRFY verifies names, EXPN expands lists, and recipient responses may distinguish mailboxes. Servers may deliberately suppress or blur these signals.
p: A command's availability does not guarantee useful enumeration.

q: Which SSH hardening change preserves modern SSH while removing an obsolete protocol?
a: Disable SSHv1 and retain a supported SSHv2 configuration
d: Disable SSHv1 and SSHv2 on the same listener
Use a non-default port instead of host-key validation
Permit root password logins to avoid key management
e: SSHv1 should be disabled. Modern SSH uses version 2; changing the port does not replace validation or access controls.
p: Disabling every protocol is not a usable SSH configuration.

q: Which description best fits a Windows access control list?
a: A collection of access-control entries for principals and rights
d: A symmetric key shared by all users of an object
A directory of every installed application
A list of the computer's TCP sockets
e: DACLs govern allowed/denied access and SACLs describe auditing. Entries bind principals to rights; ACLs do not themselves encrypt data.
p: Access control and encryption are separate protections.

q: What does a registry contain?
a: Information, settings, and options for programs installed.
d: User data and multimedia files
System logs and error reports
Network traffic statistics
Temporary internet files
e: The registry holds configuration, settings and options for installed programs and the OS.

q: What two basic elements does a registry contain?
a: Keys (similar to folders) and values (similar to files)
d: Permissions and access lists
Data packets and network headers
User profiles and system logs
Configurations and templates
e: The registry is built from keys (like folders) and values (like files).

q: Which transport and port conventionally serve WHOIS?
a: TCP/43
d: UDP/43
TCP/53
UDP/53
e: Traditional WHOIS uses TCP/43. Modern registration lookup may instead use HTTPS-based RDAP.
p: Identify the lookup protocol rather than assuming all registry access is WHOIS.

q: Which UDP port pair is used by conventional DHCPv4 server and client endpoints, respectively?
a: 67 and 68
d: 68 and 67
69 and 68
e: DHCPv4 servers use 67 and clients use 68. DHCPv6 uses 547 for servers and 546 for clients; 69 is TFTP's initial request port.
p: Check both the IP version and direction.

q: Which UDP port receives initial TFTP requests?
a: 69/UDP
d: 21/TCP
25/TCP
137/UDP
161/UDP
e: TFTP uses UDP port 69.

q: Which ports conventionally serve Kerberos authentication and Kerberos password-change services, respectively?
a: 88 TCP/UDP and 464 TCP/UDP
d: 464 TCP/UDP and 88 TCP/UDP
389 TCP and 636 TCP
135 TCP and 445 TCP
e: Kerberos authentication uses 88; password-change services use 464. LDAP and SMB use other ports and have distinct functions.
p: Authentication and password change are separate service endpoints.

q: Which TCP port pair conventionally serves POP3 and POP3 over implicit TLS?
a: 110/TCP, 995/TCP - SSL/TLS port, also known as POP3S
d: 25/TCP, 587/TCP
443/TCP, 993/TCP
21/TCP, 22/TCP
389/TCP, 636/TCP
e: POP3 uses TCP 110 (and 995 for POP3S over TLS).

q: Which port pair conventionally identifies IMAP and IMAP over implicit TLS?
a: 143 TCP and 993 TCP
d: 110 TCP and 995 TCP
25 TCP and 465 TCP
119 TCP and 563 TCP
e: IMAP uses 143 and implicit-TLS IMAP uses 993. The other pairs are POP3, SMTP, and NNTP. STARTTLS can upgrade the plaintext-port connection.
p: A protocol pair must match both service and transport.

q: Which TCP port conventionally serves BGP?
a: 179/TCP
d: 53/TCP
22/TCP
25/TCP
110/TCP
e: BGP uses TCP port 179.

q: Which port pair conventionally identifies LDAP and LDAP over implicit TLS?
a: 389 TCP and 636 TCP
d: 88 TCP and 464 TCP
445 TCP and 139 TCP
143 TCP and 993 TCP
e: LDAP commonly uses TCP/389, with StartTLS possible there; implicit TLS uses TCP/636. AD may also use UDP/389 for connectionless LDAP discovery.
p: A port alone does not prove that TLS is negotiated or validated.

q: Which TCP port sequence conventionally serves rexec, rlogin, and rsh, respectively?
e: rexec, rlogin and rsh use TCP ports 512, 513 and 514.

q: Which statement about implicit FTPS is accurate?
a: Its control connection commonly uses TCP/990; data uses a separate connection
d: It uses TCP/989 for both commands and all data
It is the same protocol as SFTP over TCP/22
It removes FTP's need for data-channel firewall handling
e: Implicit FTPS commonly uses 990 for control; explicit FTPS upgrades on 21. FTP has separate data connections, whose ports depend on mode. SFTP is an SSH subsystem.
p: FTPS and SFTP are different protocols.

q: What is SQL Server Browser's conventional network role?
a: Map instance discovery requests to instance connection details
d: Execute arbitrary commands as every database login
Store all Windows domain password hashes
Encrypt HTTP responses from the application
e: Browser commonly uses UDP/1434 for instance discovery. A named instance can listen on a dynamically selected TCP port.
p: Discovery service and database data connection are different flows.

q: What are the standardized UDP ports for RADIUS authentication and accounting, respectively?
d: 49 and 50
e: 1812/1813 are the standardized pair. 1645/1646 appear in older deployments, so an unqualified 'what ports does RADIUS use' is ambiguous.
p: A valid legacy configuration is not a wrong answer to an unqualified question.

q: Which port conventionally serves NFS?
e: NFS uses TCP/UDP port 2049.

q: Which TCP port conventionally serves PostgreSQL?
e: PostgreSQL uses TCP 5432.

q: If an X server exposes traditional TCP transport, which port conventionally corresponds to display :1?
e: Traditional X TCP ports are 6000 plus the display number. 177 is XDMCP; 5901 is associated with VNC display conventions. Many X servers disable TCP listening.
p: Check the display number and whether the transport is enabled.

q: Which group consists of first-hop redundancy protocols?
a: HSRP (Hot Standby Router Protocol), VRRP (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol), GLBP (Gateway Load Balancing Protocol)
d: OSPF, BGP, EIGRP
RIP, OSPF, EIGRP
RADIUS, TACACS+, GLBP
HSRP, BGP, EIGRP
e: The three FHRP protocols are HSRP, VRRP and GLBP.

q: Which description best distinguishes a stream cipher from a block cipher?
a: It combines plaintext units with a generated keystream
d: It must encrypt exactly one bit per API call
It requires a separate RSA key for every byte
It cannot be used with network protocols
e: Stream ciphers commonly process bytes or larger units using a keystream. One-bit-at-a-time wording is too restrictive. Reusing the same keystream can expose relationships between messages.
p: Stream operation does not mandate a one-bit interface.

q: In legacy IKEv1 PSK authentication, why is Aggressive Mode a useful offline-guessing target?
a: Captured authentication material for PSK guessing
d: The exchange sends the PSK itself in plaintext
The exchange removes Diffie-Hellman from every handshake
The exchange encrypts identity before choosing the PSK
e: Captured authentication material can support offline guesses for weak PSKs. It is not the same as reading a plaintext key. Main Mode hides more identity/authentication material.
p: A cracking verifier and a plaintext secret are different artifacts.

q: What service does TCP normally provide to an application?
a: An ordered reliable byte stream
d: An ordered reliable sequence of application messages
Encrypted and authenticated delivery by default
A guarantee that each write becomes one packet
e: TCP is a byte stream: writes and packets need not align with application records. Applications must define message framing; encryption is supplied by higher layers such as TLS.
p: Reliable delivery does not preserve message boundaries.

q: Why is 'UDP is always faster than TCP' an unsafe generalization?
a: Workload-dependent performance with different guarantees
d: UDP performs a longer handshake than TCP
TCP has no congestion control and therefore always wins
UDP guarantees retransmission so it is always more efficient
e: UDP has lower transport machinery but applications may add reliability and congestion handling. Latency and throughput depend on conditions; neither protocol is universally faster.
p: A feature tradeoff is not a universal performance ranking.

q: Where is CSMA/CD relevant in Ethernet?
a: Shared or half-duplex Ethernet, where collisions can occur
d: Full-duplex switched links as their normal access method
Wireless Ethernet as the same mechanism as CSMA/CA
Only the IP routing layer above the Ethernet frames
e: CSMA/CD detects and handles collisions on shared/half-duplex Ethernet. Full-duplex switched links do not use collision detection as their normal access mechanism.
p: Legacy shared media and modern full duplex have different behavior.

q: What belongs in penetration-test rules of engagement?
a: Scope, permitted methods, constraints, and escalation
d: Only the final severity rankings
Only the scanner's default settings
Only the customer's public address range
e: RoE defines the operating agreement, including testing windows and contacts. A target inventory is only one component.
p: A scope list alone is not a complete operating agreement.

q: What primarily distinguishes white-box from black-box assessment?
a: The internal information provided to the tester
d: Whether the test is lawful
Whether all tests are automated
Whether the application uses TLS
e: White-box testing provides internal information such as source and configuration. Either format can be authorized and can use manual and automated work.
p: Information access and testing technique are different dimensions.

q: What is the principal client benefit of a penetration test?
a: Evidence about exploitable weaknesses and improvement priorities
d: A guarantee that no vulnerability remains
Automatic certification of legal compliance
A replacement for ongoing patch management
e: A bounded assessment can expose and contextualize weaknesses. It cannot exhaust every future attack or replace continuing controls.
p: A useful assessment does not imply a security guarantee.

q: Which UK statute principally addresses unauthorized access to computer material?
a: Computer Misuse Act 1990
d: Human Rights Act 1998
Data Protection Act 2018
Freedom of Information Act 2000
e: The CMA addresses specified computer misuse offenses. Privacy and personal-data obligations arise through other legal frameworks as well.
p: Choose the law matching the conduct, not just any security-related law.

q: Which CMA section concerns unauthorized acts intended, or reckless as to, impairing computer operation?
a: Section 3
d: Section 1
Section 2
Section 3A
e: Section 3 addresses impairment-related acts. Sections 1 and 2 address unauthorized access and further-offense intent; section 3A concerns articles for specified offenses.
p: Access, impairment, and tool-related offenses differ.

q: What is the purpose of estimating testing resources during scoping?
a: Align effort with assets, objectives, and available time
d: Set severity before evidence is collected
Guarantee every host will be compromised
Make vulnerability validation unnecessary
e: Resource planning helps set a credible coverage and timescale. It does not predefine technical outcomes.
p: Effort estimates describe work, not guaranteed findings.

q: What is residual risk?
a: Risk remaining after controls are applied
d: Risk assessed before controls exist
Risk transferred without any remaining consequence
Risk eliminated by the report's publication
e: Controls reduce or modify risk; residual risk remains for further treatment or acceptance.
p: Risk treatment does not necessarily eliminate risk.

q: Which risk can testing itself introduce?
a: Service disruption or unintended data exposure
d: Only risks already present before testing
Only inaccurate scanner branding
Only changes in the client's marketing budget
e: Testing actions can affect availability, confidentiality, and integrity. Plan limits, escalation, evidence handling, and recovery.
p: The assessment process has its own operational risks.

q: Who is the executive summary primarily written to inform?
a: Decision-makers about business risk and priorities
d: Only exploit developers reproducing shellcode
Only network tools parsing machine-readable output
Only the tester's personal revision notes
e: An executive summary connects major findings to business consequences and decisions. Reproduction detail belongs in supporting technical findings.
p: A report needs different levels of detail for different readers.

q: Why retain structured notes during a test?
a: Support accurate reporting and reproducible findings
d: Replace evidence with memory of tool output
Increase the number of severity labels
Prove every scanner warning is exploitable
e: Record actions, identity, time, observations, and interpretation as work proceeds. This supports verification and avoids retrospective invention.
p: A remembered conclusion is weaker than retained causal evidence.

q: Which evidence set best supports a reproducible authorization finding?
a: Caller role, affected object, request/response, impact, and remediation
d: Tool name, screenshot, and a severity number only
A list of CVE identifiers unrelated to the application
A raw packet capture without timestamps or interpretation
e: An authorization flaw needs its identity and object context plus observable behavior. Tools and captures can supplement, but do not replace the causal explanation.
p: A useful finding connects evidence to its claim.

q: What is a useful purpose of the final debrief?
a: Explain findings, limitations, and remediation priorities
d: Expand scope after all testing is complete
Replace the written report with oral claims
Promise the environment is permanently secure
e: A debrief lets stakeholders question conclusions and understand next actions. It complements the durable report.
p: Communication and evidence should support one another.

q: How can different messages for unknown user and wrong password weaken login security?
a: They reveal account-existence signals
d: They increase the password's entropy
They prove the session cookie is predictable
They disable the need for MFA
e: An attacker may distinguish existing accounts. Messages, timing, and other observable differences all merit review.
p: A generic message alone may not remove every enumeration signal.

q: Which pair combines two different authentication factor categories?
a: Hardware token and memorized PIN
d: Password and security-question answer
Fingerprint and iris scan
Username and account number
e: Possession plus knowledge is two categories. Two knowledge checks or two biometrics are not two different factor categories.
p: More prompts are not necessarily more factors.

q: An authenticated user changes invoice=123 to invoice=124 and receives another user's private invoice. Which control failed?
a: Object-level authorization
d: Password complexity enforcement
TLS hostname validation
CSRF token generation
e: Authentication identifies the caller. The server must separately check that caller's permission for the selected object. Random IDs reduce guessing but do not replace access checks.
p: Being logged in is not permission to access every record.

q: What does an allowlist validation strategy do?
a: Permit input matching explicitly allowed forms
d: Reject only substrings already seen in attacks
Treat all client-generated data as trusted
Guarantee correct authorization for every request
e: An allowlist defines acceptable syntax or values. It complements, rather than replaces, context-aware output handling and permission checks.
p: Validation and authorization solve different problems.

q: Why must important input constraints be enforced on the server?
a: A client can submit requests without the normal browser validation
d: The browser always converts all input to SQL
TLS removes every client-side validation rule
Only a proxy can ever change a hidden field
e: Custom requests can bypass normal client code. Enforce business and syntax constraints where the trusted action happens.
p: Client convenience checks are not the authoritative boundary.

q: Which disclosure is a detailed application stack trace likely to contain?
a: Internal code paths and component details
d: Every user's current password
The TLS client's private signing key
The complete router forwarding table
e: Paths, class names, versions, and query information can assist later testing. Actual disclosure depends on the trace.
p: An error message is useful evidence without proving every possible impact.

q: Which outcome can SQL injection directly enable when the DB account can read sensitive tables?
a: Unauthorized retrieval of those tables' data
d: Automatic elevation to kernel privileges
Automatic bypass of every MFA deployment
Mandatory decryption of all external TLS sessions
e: Query manipulation can expose data reachable by the connection's rights. Other outcomes require additional permissions and mechanisms.
p: Tie claimed impact to the actual database authority.

q: Which structure is directly manipulated in LDAP search-filter injection?
a: The directory search filter's expression
d: The browser's CSS stylesheet
The SQL Server connection pool
The Ethernet frame checksum
e: LDAP filters have their own operators and escaping rules. SQL escaping is not an interchangeable defense.
p: Escaping is interpreter- and context-specific.

q: What authority is commonly abused by a successful CSRF attack?
a: The victim browser's automatically attached credentials
d: The attacker's knowledge of the victim's password
The resolver's DNSSEC signing key
The database's backup encryption key
e: The browser can send a user's cookies with a request initiated elsewhere. Origin checks, suitable tokens, and cookie policy help constrain this.
p: An attacker need not read a credential to exploit its automatic use.

q: What is the central failure in session fixation?
a: A known pre-login identifier stays valid after authentication
d: An invalid password is accepted because of a DNS error
The browser cannot read an HttpOnly cookie
The server uses a different session ID after logout
e: The identity transition should rotate and appropriately retire session identifiers. A fixed pre-login token can otherwise become authenticated.
p: Consider the transition between anonymous and authenticated state.

q: Which property most directly resists session-token guessing?
a: Unpredictability from secure random generation
d: A long but sequential account-number prefix
Base64 encoding of the user's email address
A timestamp formatted with punctuation
e: A long representation is not necessarily high entropy. Predictable input remains predictable when encoded.
p: Length and unpredictability are different properties.

q: What protection does Base64 alone provide for a secret value?
a: None against a reader who can decode it
d: Confidentiality equivalent to symmetric encryption
Integrity equivalent to a keyed HMAC
Authentication equivalent to a digital signature
e: Base64 changes representation and is reversible without a secret key. Access controls and actual cryptography address other properties.
p: An unfamiliar encoding is not secret-key protection.

q: A token is 32 hexadecimal characters long. What can its length alone establish?
a: 128 represented bits; generation method unknown
d: It is definitely an MD5 digest
It is definitely a secure session identifier
It is definitely an unsalted password hash
e: Each hex character represents four bits. Many hashes, random tokens, and truncated values can have this representation. Entropy depends on generation, not display length.
p: Representation is not algorithm identification or entropy proof.

q: A private service uses a self-signed certificate explicitly pinned by its clients. What is the correct assessment?
a: Evaluate pin distribution and identity validation
d: Self-signing proves that encryption is disabled
A public CA certificate would prevent SQL injection
Certificate pinning means expiry can always be ignored
e: A securely distributed pin can authenticate a private service. Test how trust is established and maintained; encryption, identity, and lifecycle checks are distinct.
p: A self-signed certificate is not automatically an exploitable vulnerability.

q: A threat model identifies a privileged backend trusting an unvalidated userId from the browser. What should testing prioritize?
a: Whether the caller can select another user's authority or data
d: Whether CSS rules conceal the userId field
Whether the user's browser cache is enabled
Whether the backend's logo is served over HTTPS
e: The trust boundary is where client-controlled identity influences privileged actions. Cosmetic hiding and unrelated transport details do not validate that boundary.
p: Use architecture to select a testable abuse case.

q: What useful evidence can source review add to black-box testing?
a: Internal data flows, checks, and unexposed paths
