p: Enumeration has a search boundary.

q: After a reset, a second login using the old password still succeeds. Which test distinguishes real persistence from a cached page?
a: Perform a fresh authentication with the old credential
d: Reload the reset confirmation page
Reuse a session authenticated before the reset
Compare the old and new passwords' lengths
e: Verify authentication against the server rather than a previously authenticated session or cached view.
p: A live session does not prove an old password remains valid.

q: An Oracle object privilege is granted WITH GRANT OPTION. What additional ability does that confer?
a: Granting that object privilege onward
d: Granting every unrelated system privilege
Acquiring SYSDBA authentication automatically
Changing the object's filesystem owner
e: Grant option permits delegation of the granted object privilege under applicable rules.
p: Permission delegation expands who can receive access.

q: A sort column cannot be represented as a SQL value parameter. What is a suitable design?
a: Map permitted names to fixed identifiers
d: Bind the column name as an ordinary string value
HTML-encode the column name before concatenation
Remove apostrophes but accept arbitrary expressions
e: Identifiers and values have different roles. Select fixed known columns through an allowlist mapping.
p: Value parameterization does not parameterize query structure.

q: A staff record was accessed to demonstrate excessive read access. Which later use is a different processing purpose?
a: Using it in unrelated marketing analysis
d: Using minimal protected proof in the agreed finding
Explaining the affected authorization rule
Recording the test's timing and role
e: Permission and lawful handling for assessment do not automatically extend to unrelated reuse. Purpose limitation matters.
p: An authorized collection can still have restricted later uses.

q: A firewall rule narrows who can reach a vulnerable service. What should a finding distinguish?
a: Reduced exposure from removal of the software flaw
d: That the code defect was necessarily repaired
That all insiders are unable to reach it
That every application credential is now stronger
e: A compensating restriction can reduce likelihood while leaving the vulnerability present for allowed or alternate paths.
p: A mitigation and a root-cause fix can be different states.

q: A packet capture records only a non-initial IP fragment. What transport information may be absent?
a: The original transport header and port fields
d: The IP version field necessarily
Every source and destination address
The existence of any fragment offset
e: Transport headers normally begin in the initial fragment. Reassembly and capture completeness affect interpretation.
p: A packet fragment may not be a whole transport message.

q: Can a MySQL parameter marker replace an arbitrary table name in a prepared SQL statement?
a: No; markers represent data values in permitted positions
d: Yes; a table identifier is an ordinary bound string value
Yes; markers replace arbitrary SQL keywords
Yes; binding a sort expression permits any submitted syntax
e: Use fixed mappings for permitted identifiers and bind data values through the correct API.
p: Query structure and query data need different treatment.

q: How does LOAD DATA LOCAL differ from server-side file loading?
a: LOCAL can involve a file on the client host
d: LOCAL always reads a server-host file
LOCAL makes the client irrelevant to file handling
LOCAL requires the file to be inside the server data directory
e: Review both server and client settings and the trust of the database endpoint for client-side file access.
p: The word local refers to the client in this feature.

q: A low-privilege account can modify a script in SYSVOL that runs for administrators. Which trust boundary is threatened?
a: Low-privilege write into higher-privilege execution
d: Browser rendering into DNS delegation
SMTP relay into TLS certificate validation
Anonymous FTP into wireless authentication
e: The script's consumers and execution context matter. An expected read share can become dangerous with unauthorized write access.
p: Assess who can write and who later executes.

q: A stolen active session can change the account's password without any further check. Which control best limits this action?
a: Reauthentication for sensitive changes
d: Rotation of the session only at initial login
An idle timeout that active requests continually renew
A CSRF token that accepts requests from the stolen session
e: A fresh authentication check reduces reliance on possession of an existing session for high-impact changes.
p: A hidden menu does not protect its endpoint.

q: Session cookies are HttpOnly. Why can same-origin XSS still harm an authenticated user?
a: Scripts can perform actions using the browser session
d: HttpOnly makes every cookie publicly readable
The browser must disable all request headers
The attacker automatically knows the password
e: Cookie read protection does not stop malicious script from interacting with accessible application functions.
p: Protecting cookie values is only one layer.

q: Why distinguish internal and external infrastructure assessment positions?
a: Their routes, trust assumptions, and accessible services differ
d: Internal tests cannot identify vulnerabilities
External tests automatically include every private subnet
Both positions necessarily produce identical port states
e: A vantage point changes observed exposure and plausible attack paths. Report which position supports each conclusion.
p: Reachability is contextual.

q: An API returns user text in application/json. Does finding angle brackets there prove XSS?
a: No; execution depends on subsequent handling
d: Yes; recognizable payload syntax proves execution
Yes; JSON text is automatically evaluated as HTML
No; JSON values can never reach an unsafe DOM sink
e: Raw JSON text is not automatically HTML execution. Trace whether a client later inserts values into unsafe sinks.
p: Assess the whole data flow.

q: A share grants Full Control but NTFS grants the user read-only access. What is the usual combined result for that network access?
a: The more restrictive effective access applies
d: Share Full Control overrides all NTFS restrictions
NTFS checks are bypassed over SMB
The user receives SYSTEM automatically
e: Share and filesystem permissions constrain different layers of access. Group/deny entries and effective-access details still matter.
p: One permissive layer does not erase another restrictive layer.

q: A response contains Location: /login. What kind of reference is it?
a: A relative reference resolved against request context
d: A complete DNS zone-transfer instruction
A literal filesystem path on every client
An encrypted username hidden in the header
e: Location may use relative references. Its meaning is a URI reference, not necessarily a server filesystem location.
p: URL paths and filesystem paths are different namespaces.

q: A cache stores a positive answer with TTL 600. After 200 seconds without refresh, what TTL is expected approximately?
a: 400 seconds
d: 600 seconds
800 seconds
2000 seconds
e: Remaining lifetime decreases with time. Requeries, replacement, and implementation policy can change the observed state.
p: A cached answer's TTL is remaining lifetime, not elapsed time.

q: To verify logout invalidation, which comparison is most direct?
a: Replay the same session credential after logout
d: Check only that the cookie disappears locally
Check only that the user sees the login form
Use a new session created after logout
e: The server should reject the former credential. Browser UI changes do not demonstrate revocation.
p: Observe authorization at the server after the state change.

q: UNION operands have equal column counts but incompatible data types. What follows?
a: The operation can still fail
d: It must always return the desired text
It changes all columns to passwords
It proves parameterized execution
e: Matching counts is not sufficient; type compatibility and DBMS conversion rules also matter.
p: Result shape includes types as well as count.

q: Why inspect file capabilities as well as SUID files on Linux?
a: Capabilities can grant selected privileged operations without UID 0
d: Only SUID can grant any privileged operation
Capabilities are a browser cookie format
A capability always grants every root privilege
e: Capabilities split privileged powers. Their actual grant, bounding conditions, and program behavior matter.
p: Privilege can be selective rather than all-or-nothing root identity.

q: A quote covers only the public website, but the mobile app uses a separate API. What should be clarified?
a: Whether API assets and workflows are part of the deliverable
d: Assume all interfaces are included by the website product name
Assume the mobile API is excluded without recording that limitation
Count mobile screens instead of identifying technical assets
e: An application can have several interfaces to the same business process. Specify assets and interfaces rather than relying on an ambiguous product name.
p: A business system may have more than one technical entry point.

q: What does the DNS AA flag relate to?
a: Whether the answer is authoritative for the queried name
d: Whether the caller is an administrator
Whether the response is encrypted
Whether a zone transfer was permitted
e: AA is an answer-authority indicator. It is not cryptographic authenticity or a user permission flag.
p: DNS header authority is not human authorization.

q: A normal user can download the admin report but cannot run the admin dashboard. How should this be classified?
a: Unauthorized access to the report
d: Full administrator takeover without other capability evidence
No issue because the admin menu is unavailable
A transport failure rather than report access
e: The accessed resource determines the supported claim. Different administrative functions can have separate controls.
p: Describe the precise resource and authority gained.

q: A SQL Server module runs with EXECUTE AS under a privileged principal. What must be assessed?
a: The module's reachable actions under that context
d: Only the caller's direct table grants
Only the module's metadata visibility
Only whether the caller can see the admin UI
e: Impersonated execution changes the authority available inside the module. Review permitted operations and unsafe dynamic construction.
p: The caller's apparent low privilege may not describe module execution.

q: A direct SELECT grant is revoked, but another role still grants SELECT. What may happen?
a: The user retains effective read access
d: Revocation also removes every role-based grant
Revocation changes the table's owner automatically
Revocation invalidates every other principal's permissions
e: Evaluate all permission paths. Removing one grant does not necessarily remove the capability.
p: Revocation must be checked against effective permissions.

q: HTML text encoding is reused for input inserted inside JavaScript source. What is wrong with this approach?
a: The output contexts have different grammars
d: JavaScript cannot contain user data
HTML encoding always signs scripts
All encoded characters are removed by TLS
e: Use context-appropriate handling or avoid dynamic executable contexts. HTML encoding is not a universal injection defense.
p: Ask which parser consumes the output next.

q: Why hash a retained evidence artifact at capture time?
a: Support later checks that its bytes have not changed
d: Authenticate the target's every statement automatically
Prove the artifact contains no secret
Encrypt the artifact for every reviewer
e: A hash pins content bytes when the reference itself is trusted. Provenance and storage access are separate requirements.
p: Content integrity alone does not establish origin or confidentiality.

q: A bound LIKE value contains %. Does wildcard matching alone prove SQL injection?
a: No; wildcard semantics differ from query-structure injection
d: Yes; every wildcard executes another statement
Yes; bound parameters cannot contain symbols
No; because SQL has no LIKE operator
e: Binding prevents the value becoming SQL structure, but search semantics may still require wildcard handling.
p: Injection safety and intended matching behavior are separate.

q: A root cron job executes a world-writable helper. What is the central escalation opportunity?
a: An unprivileged writer controls later privileged code
d: The file's name reveals the root password
Cron always ignores filesystem permissions
The helper must be reachable over SSH
e: The scheduler's identity and writable executed material form the path. Confirm timing, environment, and access conditions.
p: Follow bytes to the identity that consumes them.

q: How does SELECT on one table differ from SELECT ANY TABLE in Oracle?
a: One is object-scoped; the other is a broad system privilege
d: Both necessarily grant the same object scope
The single-object grant also delegates administration automatically
The broad system privilege is just a table alias
e: Oracle distinguishes system and object privileges. Broad ANY privileges require careful review, including documented exclusions.
p: Scope and exceptions determine the real capability.

q: A client setting labels a connection read-only. What should an assessor verify?
a: Effective server-enforced permissions
d: The client's descriptive label alone
The absence of UPDATE in one observed request
The use of a reporting-oriented driver name
e: Some settings express intent or affect routing rather than granting a strict security boundary. Verify the account's actual rights.
p: A client preference is not necessarily a server restriction.

q: In passive FTP, which party connects to the server's advertised data endpoint?
a: The client
d: The server to the client listener
The DNS resolver
The SMTP relay
e: Passive mode changes data-channel direction. The control connection and firewall rules remain separate concerns.
p: Data and control channels have different flow patterns.

q: A sensitive permission is granted to SQL Server's public database role. Who may inherit it?
a: All database users belonging to public
d: Only users with public in their account name
Only users explicitly added through a custom membership list
Only server-level administrators
e: All database users are members of public. Review its grants carefully rather than treating it as an ordinary limited group.
p: Broad default membership magnifies a grant.

q: Transparent Data Encryption protects database files at rest. What does it not inherently prevent?
a: An authorized SQL principal reading permitted data
d: The need to protect database encryption keys
The need to back up required decryption material
The ability to access data after successful authorized decryption
e: At-rest encryption does not replace access control on live database queries. Protect keys and backups appropriately.
p: Encryption addresses a particular data state and threat.

q: What is HTTP CONNECT commonly used for by a forward proxy?
a: Establishing a tunnel to a specified endpoint
d: Returning a complete database backup
Deleting every cache entry
Selecting the document's stylesheet
e: CONNECT creates a tunnel when permitted. Destination restrictions matter because proxy reachability can differ from client reachability.
p: A tunneling feature changes which endpoints may be reachable.

q: A user belongs to Administrators but a process has a restricted token. What must be assessed?
a: The process's effective token and elevation state
d: Group membership alone, ignoring the running token
The process executable's filename alone
The account's default login directory alone
e: Group membership does not fully describe the running token. UAC and process context can affect effective authority.
p: Account membership and process privilege differ.

q: What distinguishes two simultaneous TCP connections between the same client and server addresses?
a: Their source/destination ports as part of the flow tuple
d: Only the source and destination IP addresses
Only the destination port shared by both flows
Only the client network's subnet mask
e: Connections are identified by protocol and endpoint address/port information. Source ports can distinguish concurrent flows.
p: A host pair is not a complete connection identity.

q: A bulk export checks ownership only for the first requested record. What must change?
a: Authorization for every included record
d: Authorization only for the first and last records
Validation that every record identifier is numeric
One authentication check without object checks
e: Batch operations must enforce the applicable permission on all objects, not one representative.
p: One authorized item does not authorize the batch.

q: A client asks whether one business function resists account takeover. What should primarily shape the test plan?
a: The function's authentication and recovery paths
d: A fixed scan of every Internet port
The tester's preferred exploit framework alone
Only the number of public website images
e: Client objectives determine relevant paths, identities, and depth. Broad discovery can support the objective without replacing it.
p: Tools should serve the question the client needs answered.

q: An old authorization expires before a planned retest. What needs resolution?
a: Current authority for the retest's dates and actions
d: Only whether the old report is still readable
Only whether the hostname still resolves
Automatic use of any account from the earlier test
e: Authority can be time-limited and environment-specific. Establish the current agreement rather than inheriting an expired one.
p: Historical permission is not necessarily current permission.

q: An account named backup has UID 0. Which fact matters most for its Unix privilege identity?
a: The numeric UID is the root identity
d: The friendly name makes it unprivileged
The home path determines its UID
The account's comment cancels UID privileges
e: Unix identity is numeric. Names can be changed or misleading; effective runtime credentials and other controls still matter.
p: Do not substitute names for identities.

q: A historical public file contains a credential-like value. What remains to establish?
a: Its actual meaning, validity, scope, and consequence
d: That it grants current administrator access everywhere
That it is harmless because the archive is old
That every account in the organization shares it
e: A secret-looking artifact is a lead. Verify within authorization and avoid claims unsupported by the current state.
p: Credential appearance and usable authority are different facts.

q: A browser extension causes a popup during a test. Why is a clean controlled browser context useful?
a: It reduces unrelated sources of execution
d: It proves all extensions and applications share identical execution rules
It makes a popup sufficient proof without tracing input
It replaces the need to record the actual request
e: Control the environment and preserve evidence connecting input to behavior. Extension activity can confound a test.
p: An observed popup needs an attributed cause.

q: Client code reads location.search and assigns it to innerHTML. Which evidence most directly supports DOM XSS?
a: A controlled source value reaching executable markup in that sink
d: The mere presence of innerHTML in unrelated code
The marker appearing in an inert server log
A status 200 response without browser evidence
e: Trace the attacker-controlled source, transformations, and dangerous sink, then verify browser behavior.
p: A source and a sink must be connected, not merely present.

q: A mirrored discussion archive strips some headers. What should its analysis preserve?
a: The mirror provenance and missing original metadata
d: A claim that the mirror authenticates every author
A claim that all timestamps are necessarily exact
Only the archive's visual theme
e: Mirrors can alter presentation or omit context. Attribute observations to the actual retained source.
p: A convenient copy may not preserve every provenance field.

q: Which conventional RID identifies the built-in Guest account?
e: 501 identifies Guest within the relevant authority. 500 identifies the built-in Administrator; a group RID has a different role.
p: Account and group identifiers are not interchangeable.

q: Why inspect the full CNAME chain rather than only its first target?
a: Later aliases can reveal the actual dependency and failure point
d: The first alias authenticates every subsequent host
Every alias guarantees a zone-transfer permission
Only the longest name can host a service
e: Several steps can change the final endpoint. Chain contents, freshness, and provider behavior all affect interpretation.
p: A first-hop dependency may not be the final dependency.

q: A low-impact method is allowed only during a maintenance window. Does low expected impact remove that timing constraint?
a: No; the agreed window still applies
d: Yes; only destructive tests have timing constraints
Yes; a public asset has no timing conditions
No; the method becomes illegal everywhere permanently
e: Rules can constrain timing independently of expected technical impact. Use the agreed schedule and escalation path.
p: Authorization can have several simultaneous conditions.

q: Which FSMO role controls schema changes?
a: Schema Master
d: Infrastructure Master
RID Master
PDC Emulator
e: Schema changes modify definitions used by directory objects. This is a forest-wide role, distinct from RID allocation.
p: Forest-wide and domain-wide responsibilities differ.

q: Why record the authenticated principal in an authorization finding?
a: Access behavior depends on the caller's authority
d: The principal's name proves its password is strong
Every request is anonymous once stored in a report
Only TLS certificates determine user rights
e: The same operation can be valid for one role and improper for another. Preserve the role/account context.
p: A response without caller context can be ambiguous.

q: The same root control flaw affects several paths. What can a coherent report do?
a: Group the cause while listing affected cases and exceptions
d: Discard all but one affected path's existence
Invent a different cause for every URL
Count each response as an independent business breach
e: Grouping can make remediation clear without hiding breadth. Preserve distinct evidence and affected scope.
p: Consolidating presentation must not erase exposure information.

q: Why can a native web-server module's memory bug have serious impact?
a: Its code executes within the server's process context
d: It necessarily runs only as browser text
It cannot access request data
It has no relationship to server privilege
e: A module can process untrusted requests within the server. Process identity and isolation determine consequences.
p: Extension code can inherit a powerful execution environment.

q: A restrictive CSP is added while unsafe HTML insertion remains. What is the best security interpretation?
a: CSP adds defense in depth; fix the unsafe sink too
d: CSP makes all untrusted markup safe by definition
CSP replaces object authorization everywhere
CSP proves no browser can ever execute injected code
e: A policy can reduce exploitability but should not substitute for safe data handling and output controls.
p: Mitigations do not justify leaving the root cause.

q: A request returns 302. What is necessary before interpreting the final page as evidence?
a: Inspect the redirect and relevant final response
d: Treat the 302 status as proof of unauthorized access
Inspect only the final page title
Assume redirects preserve every method and credential
e: Redirection can change location, method handling, and authentication context. Preserve the chain needed to explain behavior.
p: A final page does not describe every intermediate response.

q: A client accepts any trusted certificate without checking its hostname. Which attack remains possible?
a: Impersonation using a certificate for another name
d: An expired certificate passing expiry validation
A trusted peer's certificate revealing its private key
A correctly authenticated server losing all traffic encryption
e: Chain trust and identity matching are separate checks. Validate the intended endpoint identity.
p: A trusted issuer did not certify every hostname for that certificate.

q: A server refuses AXFR but answers ordinary records. What is established?
a: Transfer access is restricted on that tested path
d: Every record in the zone is secret
The server cannot serve authoritative DNS
All DNS enumeration techniques are blocked
e: Transfer restrictions are a specific control. Ordinary lookups, other nameservers, and public artifacts provide separate visibility.
p: One denied operation is not total nondisclosure.

q: What makes XML well-formed at a basic structural level?
a: Properly nested elements with matching delimiters
d: Every element name has a public DNS record
Every document is signed with an X.509 key
Every value is encrypted using the same cipher
e: Well-formedness is a syntax property. Schema validity, trust, and safe parsing impose other requirements.
p: Syntactic correctness does not mean safe or authorized content.

q: A search snippet contains text that the current page lacks. What should be considered?
a: Index timing, alternate views, and snippet generation
d: That the current server must have been compromised
That the snippet proves a live credential
That the browser has administrator privileges
e: Search engines maintain their own representations of content. Correlate the source and retrieval times.
p: Indexed presentation can lag live content.

q: Two concurrent withdrawals both pass a balance check and overdraw the account. What is the relevant failure?
a: Non-atomic validation and update
d: A stale authorization role without concurrency effects
A SQL syntax injection demonstrated by timing alone
An invalid amount type rather than a consistency failure
e: Protect consistency with appropriate atomic operations, locking, or transaction isolation. A rule can be correct yet raced.
p: Sequential tests may miss concurrency behavior.

q: A SOAP response contains a Fault describing a server exception. What should be inspected?
a: The disclosed fault detail and its application meaning
d: Only whether HTTP status is 200 or 500
Only whether the XML is well-formed
Only whether the method was declared in the service definition
e: Faults can reveal internal details or describe operation failure. Inspect content without assuming every fault is injection evidence.
p: Protocol-defined errors can still disclose implementation information.

q: A GPO exists but is not linked to an affected OU. Why does its presence not prove enforcement?
a: Existence and application scope are different
d: Every GPO applies to every domain object
Only the file's name determines its scope
A GPO link always overrides all filtering
e: Linking, inheritance, filtering, and precedence determine application. Inventory alone is insufficient.
p: Configured objects and resultant policy are different evidence.

q: An ordinary merchant stores CVV after authorization, encrypted at rest. What is the PCI concern?
a: Encryption does not make that prohibited retention acceptable
d: Any encryption makes all payment data retention acceptable
CVV is only the cardholder's public username
PCI applies only to unencrypted network packets
e: PCI SSC explains that card verification values must not be stored after authorization by merchants, even encrypted.
p: Data-category restrictions can be stricter than an encryption requirement.

q: A PTR lookup returns a hostname. Why confirm forward resolution separately?
a: Reverse and forward zones are independently administered data
d: PTR guarantees a matching A/AAAA record
PTR is a validated login token
Reverse DNS lists every virtual host on the IP
e: Reverse naming can be stale, generic, or inconsistent. Forward checks can corroborate the relation without proving ownership.
p: A reverse name is not a complete identity assertion.

q: A bundle includes an endpoint string never reached during normal navigation. What is a useful next interpretation?
a: An unexamined functionality lead within the relevant scope
d: A guaranteed anonymous administrator endpoint
An automatic scope grant to all referenced hosts
Proof that the route executes SQL directly
e: Client code can reveal hidden workflow and obsolete routes. Confirm existence, state, and authority.
p: A string reference is not a validated live action.

q: An Oracle listener accepts a connection request. What does that alone prove?
a: Listener reachability and a handled connection attempt
d: Successful database authentication
Confirmed read access to the selected schema
Confirmed administrative database rights
e: A listener routes connections to services; database authentication and authorization are separate stages.
p: A network service reply is not a database login.

q: Which FSMO role allocates RID pools to domain controllers?
a: RID Master
d: PDC Emulator
Schema Master
Domain Naming Master
e: RID allocation helps DCs create unique security identifiers within a domain. Other roles manage different directory operations.
p: Know which single-master responsibility matches the operation.

q: An endpoint returns 429 with Retry-After. What behavior is it expressing?
a: A request-rate limit and suggested retry timing
d: A permanent deletion of the account
An instruction to disable TLS validation
A guarantee that earlier requests failed
e: 429 signals too many requests; Retry-After can guide retry timing. Assess actual enforcement scope rather than its mere presence.
p: Rate-limit scope matters: account, IP, token, and action may differ.

q: A network banner suggests an old database release. What supports a patch finding more strongly?
a: Verified build and applicable vendor advisory
d: The service using its conventional port
A product family without its build information
A scanner's guess without an applicability check
e: Version clues can be misleading or incomplete. Verify the relevant build and applicability before claiming a known vulnerability.
p: Product family is not an exact vulnerable build.

q: Why should SYSDBA access be separated from routine application access?
a: It provides powerful database administration authority
d: It is required for ordinary application SELECT queries
It limits access to the caller's own tables
It only allows inspection of listener metadata
e: Administrative authentication and privileges have substantial consequences. Routine apps should not require them.
p: An application's workload rarely needs full database administration.

q: A calculator implements user expressions with a general-purpose eval API. What is the main design concern?
a: Untrusted data is interpreted as program code
d: A failure to salt stored password hashes
A failure to enforce object ownership
A failure to rotate the login session
e: Use a constrained expression parser or permitted operations rather than general execution of untrusted code.
p: Feature requirements rarely justify a complete language interpreter.

q: A review finds a user value passed to createTextNode. What is the immediate sink behavior?
a: Creating a text node rather than parsing HTML
d: Executing the value as JavaScript
Treating the value as a SQL expression
Granting the value same-origin credentials
e: A text-node API is appropriate for text output. Trace other uses of the value independently.
p: A safe sink should be recognized as well as an unsafe one.

q: A UNION query fails because its result has two columns while the original query has three. What requirement was violated?
a: Matching column count
d: Matching table name length
Matching HTTP status number
Matching database username length
e: UNION operands must have compatible result shapes, including equal column counts and compatible types.
p: A payload can be syntactically plausible yet incompatible with the query.

q: An X-Mailer field names a product version. How should this be treated?
a: A sender-supplied fingerprint to corroborate
d: A signed guarantee of every server patch
An authorization token for the mailbox
A complete description of the delivery path
e: Client identifiers may be absent, modified, or spoofed. They can guide hypotheses without proving current applicability.
p: A claimed client version is not a verified software inventory.

q: Several files already exist on a host before testing. Which cleanup rule is most defensible?
a: Remove only identified test-owned artifacts under the agreed plan
d: Delete every suspicious-looking file
Delete the whole temporary directory regardless of ownership
Retain every newly created account indefinitely
e: Cleanup needs provenance and expected prior state. Existing or third-party artifacts should not be conflated with the test's changes.
p: Ownership must be known before deleting evidence or state.

q: A tester inventories only form fields. Which possible injection inputs are omitted?
a: Headers, cookies, paths, and API bodies
d: Only visible fields that have editable controls
Only POST fields containing apostrophes
Only parameters whose names suggest passwords
e: Applications may use many request fields as data. Identify how inputs reach processing paths rather than relying on visible forms.
p: Input location does not determine trust.

q: A historical note lists SCOTT/TIGER. What should a modern assessment infer?
a: A legacy sample-account lead to verify, not a guaranteed login
d: The historical credential proves a present unlocked login
Presence of a sample schema proves its password is unchanged
An old sample-account name proves SYSDBA access
e: Installation, release, sample schemas, account locking, and authentication differ. Avoid asserting universal defaults.
p: Historical knowledge guides a check; it does not replace evidence.

q: A user-controlled value is inserted into an LDAP distinguished name. Which defense matches this sink?
a: DN-specific escaping and validation
d: SQL parameter binding alone
JavaScript string escaping alone
Replacing only HTML angle brackets
e: Distinguished-name values have grammar rules separate from LDAP filters. Handle them with the corresponding safe mechanism.
p: One LDAP escaping routine is not automatically suitable everywhere.

q: An error reveals C:\inetpub\site\config. What has been disclosed?
a: A likely server-side path and platform clue
d: Proof that the path is remotely writable
The administrator's valid password
A complete list of virtual-host permissions
e: Paths can help correlate environment and test hypotheses. Existence, readability, and writability are separate properties.
p: A path disclosure is not a file-access primitive.

q: A flaw allows unauthorized object access despite random IDs. Which recommendation addresses the cause?
a: Enforce object authorization for the caller
d: Add more random characters to IDs only
Change the page's visible button text only
Move the endpoint to a less obvious path only
e: Unpredictable identifiers can reduce discovery but do not establish access permission. Remediate the missing decision.
p: Obscurity should not replace the root control.

q: A process API passes arguments directly without a shell. Why can untrusted input still be dangerous?
a: It may supply harmful options to the program
d: It must always be parsed as shell syntax
It automatically receives filesystem isolation
It can no longer contain spaces
e: Removing the shell reduces shell injection, but argument injection remains possible. Validate allowable values and option handling.
p: No shell does not mean no dangerous interpretation.

q: An application uses an Access .accdb file in a shared folder. What boundary deserves particular attention?
a: Filesystem access to the database file
d: Only the SQL Server instance's server roles
Only an Oracle listener's remote administration policy
Only a MySQL network bind address
e: Access file deployments rely heavily on controlling the file and its copies. Do not assume a separate network database server.
p: Identify the actual deployment model before testing controls.

q: A web directory exposes .bak files containing old source and secrets. What is the relevant correction?
a: Keep sensitive backups outside served paths
d: Remove directory listings while retaining guessable backup URLs
Change the backup suffix while keeping public read access
Block POST but allow unauthenticated GET to the artifacts
e: Do not serve deployment artifacts and secrets as public content. Removing links is not access control.
p: Assess resources reachable without navigation links.

q: Why separate mailbox-user authorization from Exchange administration rights?
a: They grant different operations and resource scopes
d: Every mailbox owner is an Exchange administrator
Every administrator has every user's plaintext password
A mailbox's email address determines all server permissions
e: Administrative and end-user surfaces have different authorities. Review delegated rights and actual operations.
p: Access to one mailbox does not imply server-wide administration.

q: JSON requests are validated, but equivalent form requests enter another handler. What should an assessment cover?
a: Both accepted parsing paths
d: Only the preferred JSON path
Only the frontend's declared request type
Only the path that responds with status 200
e: Alternative encodings can invoke distinct validation or binding behavior.
p: Coverage follows accepted behavior, not the preferred client format.

q: A search engine returns no results for a company's internal host pattern. What can be concluded?
a: No matching indexed results were found with that query
d: No such hosts exist anywhere
The company has no internal network
All naming conventions are cryptographically secret
e: Indexing, syntax, freshness, and visibility limit search results. Alternative sources can provide other evidence.
p: A query's empty result has a coverage boundary.

q: An app receives privileges on shop.* rather than *.*. What does this primarily narrow?
a: Database-object scope
d: The available TCP source ports
The account's password hashing work factor
The choice of certificate authority
e: Grant scope determines which databases or objects are covered. The granted privilege types still matter.
p: Narrow scope and narrow capabilities are both needed.

q: A client lists an IP owned by a supplier but cannot describe the service agreement. What should scoping establish?
a: The authority and conditions for testing that supplier-hosted asset
d: Only that the IP responds to a TCP probe
Only the client's corporate registration number
Only that the supplier uses the same country code
e: Technical reachability and a client's request do not settle third-party testing authority. Resolve ownership and applicable permission boundaries.
p: The asset's relationship to the client must be documented.

q: Why can a distribution package's security revision matter more than its upstream banner?
a: The distribution may backport fixes
d: Banners always contain signed patch evidence
Every distribution rewrites all function names
Package metadata grants exploit permission
e: Vendor package advisories and installed revisions can establish fixes without an upstream version change.
p: Compare against the vendor's actual maintenance lineage.

q: Login returns identical text, but nonexistent users respond much faster. Which weakness remains?
a: Account enumeration through timing
d: Password spraying across several accounts
Session fixation using a known identifier
Credential stuffing using leaked passwords
e: Generic messages can still disclose account existence through repeatable timing differences. Compare controlled samples and investigate the different paths.
p: Equal text does not mean equal observable behavior.

q: A destructive proof is run successfully on a staging copy. What must a production finding state?
a: The copy's relationship to production and the validation limit
d: That production was definitely compromised by the same test
That staging evidence can never be relevant
That every environmental difference is irrelevant
e: Comparable configuration can support a strong inference. Distinguish observed copy behavior from untested production consequences.
p: A representative environment is not the same environment.

q: Why can a named-user ACL entry show more rights than the user's effective access?
a: The ACL mask may limit the effective rights
d: The entry is always ignored on Unix
The owner name necessarily overrides every ACL
The file's extension automatically removes write access
e: POSIX ACL masks constrain certain entries. Tools may show both configured and effective rights.
p: Declared rights and effective rights can differ.

q: One critical workflow could not be assessed because required access was unavailable. How should closure describe it?
a: An explicit coverage limit or unresolved item
d: A passed workflow because no flaw was observed
A confirmed vulnerability without any evidence
A completed test hidden from the client
e: Unperformed work remains a limitation, even when the rest of the engagement concludes. Explain its consequence for assurance.
p: Completion of an engagement is not proof every planned case was assessed.

q: Adding a quote causes a 500 response. What is established at this point?
a: An input-dependent error needing investigation
d: Confirmed SQL injection regardless of parser
Confirmed denial of service regardless of repeatability
Confirmed database privilege regardless of account context
e: An error may come from SQL or other parsers. Repeat and identify the failure before claiming SQL injection.
p: A common probe is not proof of its intended mechanism.

q: Why can an HTML developer comment be visible even when absent from the rendered page?
a: The browser receives it in the document source
d: The comment is necessarily sent by DNS
The comment is automatically encrypted in the DOM
The comment exists only on the server's private disk
e: Rendered presentation is not the whole received artifact. Source review can reveal paths, clues, or secrets in comments.
p: Not displayed is not the same as not delivered.

q: A technical contact email appears in registration data. Why should it not automatically be treated as an active employee account?
a: It may be an alias, role mailbox, proxy, or historical contact
d: Every contact is the current domain administrator login
Every contact carries the site's password
Registration addresses always bypass mail authentication
e: Use the address as an attribution lead. Account existence, organizational relationship, and authority require separate evidence.
p: A public contact string is not an authenticated identity.

q: A token says it expires at noon, but the server accepts it at 13:00. What must enforcement check?
a: The server's validated expiry decision and clock handling
d: Only the client's displayed expiration warning
Only the token's decoded timestamp
Only that the token has the expected field names
e: Claims need validated, server-enforced semantics and appropriate clock assumptions.
p: Readable expiry metadata is not enforced expiry.

q: A database stores login passwords with a password hash. What should be used for a secret the app must recover verbatim?
a: Appropriate encryption or secret storage
d: A one-way password verification hash
A Base64 encoding of the plaintext
A fast unkeyed checksum used as encryption
e: Password verification does not need recovery; reusable service secrets have a different requirement and need controlled recoverability.
p: Choose protection according to how the value must be used.

q: What does selecting an NNTP newsgroup primarily establish?
a: The article context for subsequent group-oriented operations
d: Administrator control of the news server
A DNS delegation to the group name
A private shell on the article author's computer
e: NNTP groups organize articles. Selection and reading permissions are separate server behavior.
p: A group identifier is a content namespace.

q: A link builder correctly quotes href but accepts script-capable schemes. Which test dimension matters?
a: URL scheme validation
d: Only safe quoting of the attribute delimiter
Only that the URL has a colon
Only that the link text contains no angle brackets
e: Evaluate the value's semantics in addition to markup syntax. Safe URL schemes are context-dependent.
p: Syntactic escaping cannot make every URL safe.
